name: Face Restoration
description: Restore detail in blurry, low-resolution faces with AI
longDescription:
Finds the faces in every frame and redraws them with a neural network trained on hundreds of thousands of portraits, so eyes, teeth and skin come back from a soft VHS or low-resolution picture. Only the face itself is replaced (not hair, neck or background), blended in at the video's own resolution, and every pixel outside the faces is left exactly as it was.

It runs after Crop & Resize, so upscaling first gives the network more to work with. A restored face is the network's best reconstruction, not the original: it can look smoother or slightly different from the person, which is what Strength is for. Faces smaller than the minimum size are left alone, since there is too little in them to restore.

The models are separate downloads. RestoreFormer++ is the default and free for any use. GFPGAN and CodeFormer are alternatives for non-commercial use only; CodeFormer adds a fidelity control. On a Mac they run on the graphics card and Neural Engine, on Windows on any DirectX 12 graphics card, and otherwise on the CPU, which is much slower.

methods.name: Face Restoration
methods.description: Detect each face, restore it with the chosen model, blend it back

ui.label: Model
ui.description: The network that redraws the faces. RestoreFormer++ is natural-looking and free for any use. GFPGAN gives stronger, more stylised detail; CodeFormer is good on very damaged faces and has a fidelity control. Both are separate downloads for non-commercial use only

ui.label: Strength
ui.description: How much of the restored face replaces the original. Lower keeps more of the real face and its texture, and flickers less

ui.label: Fidelity
ui.description: Lower trusts CodeFormer's learned faces more (cleaner, less like the person); higher stays closer to the picture. 0.5 to 0.7 suits most video

ui.label: Steady faces between frames
ui.description: Steady each face over the frames either side: its position is smoothed, one-frame gaps in detection are bridged, and the restored face is averaged with its neighbours wherever the picture is still, so detail the network invents doesn't shimmer. Turn off to restore every frame on its own

ui.label: Detection Confidence
ui.description: How sure the face detector must be. Lower finds more faces in poor pictures, and more things that are not faces

ui.label: Minimum Face Size
ui.description: Faces smaller than this many pixels are left alone: there is too little in them to restore, and the network would invent a face rather than recover one

ui.label: Maximum Faces
ui.description: Restore at most this many faces per frame, the largest first. Each face costs as much time as the next, so a crowd is slow

implementation.role: finds, aligns, restores and blends back each face (ONNX Runtime)
finds the faces and their eyes, nose and mouth
restores each face, as close to the picture as Fidelity asks
masks the blend to the face itself
blends the faces in, leaving every other pixel untouched
